headline: High-risk default write/egress overlap: Goose can hand outputs to Kestra workflows, creating dangerous prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP and reads/writes the user filesystem; Kestra can ingest files, stdin/stdout, and trigger workflows. That creates a plausible content-to-instruction bridge if Goose outputs attacker-controlled text into shared files or streams. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Goose writes untrusted content into a file or stream that Kestra later parses as workflow input
IF Kestra consumes Goose-produced artifacts without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for Goose and Kestra inputs
Require a manual review step before Kestra ingests Goose output
Prefix Goose-generated files with a non-executable extension
Disable any Kestra trigger that watches Goose output paths
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code, files in cwd, and broad network egress; Kestra handles logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, and notifications. If they share a workspace or Goose passes files into Kestra, sensitive data can flow from Goose into Kestra outputs or external destinations. The shared-file path is enough to make this medium.
conditions: IF Goose and Kestra share any writable workspace path
IF Goose forwards files containing source code or secrets into Kestra workflows
IF Kestra sends those artifacts to email, Slack, cloud storage, or other external sinks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory before execution
Restrict Kestra notifications for workflows fed by Goose
Audit one sample Goose-to-Kestra artifact for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and shell execution, and Goose explicitly shares state via filesystem while Kestra supports multiple instances and writes to /app/storage and /tmp. Concurrent modification of the same directory can corrupt files, overwrite outputs, or race on git state; Goose also modifies git state directly. This is a default-dangerous overlap, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Goose modifies git state while Kestra writes artifacts in the same repo
IF Kestra runs multiple instances against shared storage without locking
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Avoid running Goose and Kestra against the same git checkout
Check for lock files before starting either agent
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, files, and MCP-driven outputs; Kestra can execute declarative workflows and send notifications or trigger cloud actions. If Kestra treats Goose output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Goose result can cascade into emails, deployments, or data jobs. Because the downstream action surface is broad and default workflows are automation-oriented, high fits.
conditions: IF Kestra uses Goose output as workflow parameters without validation
IF Goose-produced text is mapped into Kestra tasks, notifications, or API calls
IF a Kestra workflow can act on Goose output without human approval
mitigations: Insert a validation step between Goose and Kestra
Require human approval for any Goose-derived workflow action
Limit Goose output to read-only reports
Test one workflow with a harmless dummy payload
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Goose outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model-provider keys and extension tokens on the user machine, while Kestra processes logs, notifications, cloud storage data, and database data. The profiles do not document residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated data is routed through Kestra or if Goose sends it to external model providers. Uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed from Goose into Kestra workflows
IF Kestra notifications or storage retain data longer than policy allows
IF Goose sends sensitive inputs to external model providers
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflows
Review retention settings for Kestra logs and artifacts
Disable notifications for sensitive workflows
Confirm model-provider handling for Goose secrets
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
